transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-15 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan, Anika, Marco (Redwood) — Priya, Liam, Sofia, Aaron (Fairwind)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm Jordan with Redwood, i'm the AE, um quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya: hey, priya here, head of platform at fairwind, thanks.
[00:15] Liam: liam, devops, morning everyone.
[00:19] Sofia: sofia, data eng.
[00:21] Aaron: aaron, security.
[00:23] Anika: anika, csm at redwood. excited to kick this off.
[00:28] Jordan: cool, objective for today is sprint zero immersion — align deliverables, security knobs, and agree on first benchmark window. we'll keep it tight 45–60 min, actionable next steps.

[00:45] Marco: great, i'll lead the technical bits. i want to get a sense of your current inference flow — are you calling models via a hosted api now or running in-house?
[00:56] Priya: right now we do a mix; we have some calls to openai for summarization and a self-hosted triton cluster for internal rerank models. latency's been... inconsistent, and cost is creeping. primary use case is real-time ETA/dispatch assistant in the app — 200–600 rps during peak, 30k tokens per minute roughly.
[01:20] Marco: got it. a key thing with redwood is we can run hosted, dedicated reserved pools, or private in your vpc. for an enterprise with data residency and SOC2 needs you mentioned, dedicated or private usually fits.
[01:34] Priya: yeah we need to keep PII in our VPC, at least for the pilot.
[01:38] Aaron: and we have an upcoming SOC2 Type II audit in q3, so audit logs, kms integration, key rotation, and retention policies are important.
[01:48] Jordan: good note. anika, can we share the compliance pack and ksm—kms integration sample after the call?
[01:55] Anika: yes, i'll attach the SOC2 docs, KMS integration guide, and SAML primer.

[02:10] Liam: on network side, we prefer VPC peering with strict CIDR allow-lists and no public egress for tokens. is private deployment fully air-gapped?
[02:22] Marco: depends on the package — private on-prem can be air-gapped; vpc deployments still use a customer-controlled peering but the control plane communication is optional. we have a private control-plane option that keeps inference nodes in your subnets. i'll share the topology diagrams.
[02:37] Sofia: for data, we do token masking and PII redaction upstream, but want assurance that logs won't leak training data.
[02:45] Marco: we support token-level opt-out and KV cache eviction policies. logs can be sent to your syslog/siem and we can disable user-text retention in the tenant.

[03:05] Jordan: let's pivot to success criteria — what does fairwind want out of pilot?
[03:10] Priya: three things: 1) verifiable latency under 150ms p95 for the dispatch path at 500 rps steady; 2) authorization and SSO working with our IDP; 3) audit logs for any request referencing PII. if those pass, we'll expand to 10k monthly active drivers.
[03:28] Jordan: sensible. does that map to a month-long pilot?
[03:31] Priya: yes, target to start pilot first week of june and complete by end of june, so get sprint zero done next two weeks.

[03:45] Marco: for the latency target, we'll need a performance baseline. can you share a traffic profile and token distribution? small prompts vs large prompts change batching behavior.
[03:56] Sofia: sure, i'll export a week of anonymized requests and synthetic profiles. expect a bimodal distribution — short 12–20 token prompts for ETA and 200–600 token prompts for driver summaries.
[04:12] Marco: perfect. we'll use that to pick batching window, KV cache policy, and quantization profile. also need to know acceptable quality delta if we apply int8 quantization — some teams accept slight BLEU/perp delta for cost wins.
[04:26] Priya: cost is a factor but quality can't degrade dispatch-critical decisions. so minimal regressions only.
[04:31] Jordan: noted. we'll propose a model variant matrix: one high-quality (float16) for critical path, one quantized for background tasks.

[04:45] Aaron: encryption — how does redwood integrate with KMS? we use aws-kms and with HSM-backed keys for sensitive ops.
[04:53] Marco: we integrate via envelope encryption. customers provide a KMS ARN; data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys. for control plane metadata we offer optional host-side encryption. i'll share the design doc.
[05:06] Aaron: also need certificate rotation policy and proof of key separation in the architecture.
[05:11] Marco: yes, that's in the doc.

[05:25] Anika: operations questions — what does your runbook look like? who will be primary contacts?
[05:31] Priya: me for platform, liam for infra, aaron for security, sofia for data. we'll create a slack channel for the pilot.
[05:38] Anika: great. i'll set up the channel and weekly 30-minute standups starting 2026-05-25.

[05:50] Jordan: ok timeline recap: share sprint-zero checklist and onboarding deck by monday 5/18; marcos to run a synthetic baseline by 5/20; you provide traffic/profile + VPC diagram by 5/22; pilot target start wk of june 1. does that sound right?
[06:06] Priya: yes. question — what kind of metrics dashboard do you provide out of the box? we need token-level cost, latency per route, and per-tenant audit logs.
[06:18] Marco: redwood console has per-route latency and cost, token breakdowns, and you can export traces to your observability stack. we also provide a webhook stream of events for audit logs.
[06:28] Sofia: can we push logs to our splunk?
[06:30] Marco: yes, we support syslog/forwarders and S3 export.

[06:42] Liam: about fallbacks — if the dedicated pool is saturated, do you have automatic degradation? we don't want end-users blocked.
[06:50] Jordan: we have smart routing and fallbacks; for pilot we can configure a cheaper/compatible model to serve non-critical work or queue requests with graceful retry.
[06:59] Priya: good. also curious on how rollouts work — can we do canary by percentage?
[07:04] Marco: yes, canary and A/B rollouts are supported in config, also automatic fallback on error thresholds.

[07:18] Aaron: security question — who has access to the logs and console? we need RBAC, SSO, and audit trails.
[07:25] Anika: we support SAML SSO and granular RBAC. we'll give tenant-admin roles to you and a read-only to executives.
[07:34] Aaron: also need proof of pen test history and data deletion flow for customers.
[07:39] Jordan: we'll send a security pack including historical pen test dates, SOC2 paperwork, and data deletion procedures.

[07:52] Priya: what about billing visibility? we want near real-time spend dashboards per route.
[07:58] Marco: console shows token spend with hourly granularity. for reserved dedicated capacity we overlay committed usage and burst costs.
[08:08] Priya: ok that's helpful.

[08:18] Jordan: any blockers to getting the sample traffic and VPC diagram?
[08:23] Sofia: none, i'll get the anonymized payloads and token histograms to you by 5/22. i might scrub some domain names which could slightly alter distribution but we'll note that.
[08:34] Liam: also will need a test account in your staging environment to peer. how do you handle peering approval turnarounds?
[08:41] Marco: we usually request a temporary jump host for testing; once peering IPs and security groups are shared we can do a short window test. typical turnarounds are 48–72 hours.

[08:55] Anika: i'll schedule the weekly slot and send calendar invites for the sprint ceremonies.
[09:00] Jordan: ok, let's call out explicit success criteria for the pilot: 1) p95 latency < 150ms for dispatch path at 500 rps; 2) SSO/SAML integration complete; 3) audit logs collected and verified by aaron; 4) documentation of key management and retention policies.
[09:16] Priya: agreed. one more thing — can you run a small quality regression test comparing the quantized path vs float16 for our summarization prompts?
[09:25] Marco: yes, we'll run an A/B with a small prompt set and provide metrics (ROUGE/perp) and subjective examples.

[09:36] Jordan: perfect. any other questions?
[09:39] Aaron: we'll need a security contact at redwood for SOC2 clarifications — who should i email?
[09:44] Jordan: cc anika and marco, and i'll include our security lead (emma cole) in the pack.
[09:50] Anika: noted.

[09:55] Jordan: recap of next steps — i'll share the sprint zero checklist + onboarding deck, marco will schedule the benchmark run and share the topology doc, sofia will send traffic samples, aaron will confirm KMS/encryption requirements. anika to set up the cadence. we'll reconvene next week after the baseline results.
[10:16] Priya: thanks everyone, this was helpful. looking forward to the run.
[10:19] Jordan: thanks all.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present in audio; product names sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'Redwood Dedicated pool' inconsistently. timestamps are approximate.
